text:
maria_eng: quick sync — thinking about splitting the Dedicated autoscaler into two bounded services: an "intent"/policy decision service and an "executor" that talks to the pool operator. tradeoffs?

sam-runtime: +1. main wins are smaller blast radius for autoscaler logic changes and clearer ownership between decisioning and allocation.

josh: concerned about the fast burst lane. if decisioning is async we might add latency when tenants need immediate capacity. is a local fast-path cache required?

elaine: also worried about billing + accounting. if intent is accepted but executor fails to allocate, we need idempotent guarantees so tenants aren't billed for phantom allocations.

maria_eng: proposed end-to-end flow:
```
client -> intent-service (validate policy, reserve intent token) -> write intent to durable log
executor watches log, tries allocate GPUs from pool-operator -> writes allocation status (allocated/failed)
billing reads final allocations from executor status stream
```
This keeps decisioning deterministic and executor focused on side effects.

sam-runtime: add admission TTL + optimistic prewarm tokens so executor can map a token->quick allocation without re-querying policy on hot paths. tokens can be reclaimed.

josh: prewarm tokens are good. idea: two allocation classes: soft (prewarm/spot-like, reclaimable) and hard (reserved, billed). executor should expose both.

elaine: agree. also need a reconcile/finalizer loop: every intent has idempotency key + finalizer to avoid orphaned gpus if executor crashes mid-alloc. billing should only charge once finalizer cleared.

autoscaler-bot: Notice: pool gpool-7 scaled +2 GPUs to meet tenant:acme-burst request (op-id op-5991) :white_check_mark:

devops: ops note: ensure allocate_gpu() has a 5s connect timeout and exponential backoff; we've hit long hangs when the operator API stalls. also surface metric `intent->alloc latency` in console.

maria_eng: ok can someone own two small followups before design doc: 1) API proto for intent->executor events (watch + ack semantics) 2) runbook: rollback when partial failure (intent accepted but allocation timed out). i'll drive these in the sprint.

josh: i'll draft the proto and push an initial protobuf/REST sketch to git.

elaine: i'll draft the rollback runbook and include billing edge cases.

maria_eng: thanks! :thumbsup:
